notes: Single source of truth for the native numerical-correctness contract.
The rendered table in docs/ggml-engine.md is GENERATED from this file
(uv run python tests/parity_contract.py --write-docs) and a test fails on drift.
Required-target semantics per environment: assets present + zero tests executed
= FAIL (skip-vacuum); assets absent = distinct UNAVAILABLE report that only
fails under STARLING_PARITY_STRICT=1; a present asset whose sha256 differs
from the pin = FAIL (never measure or silently regenerate a reference).
backend status 'validated' means: this contract was measured passing on that
backend against THIS entry's pinned reference revision. Anything else is
'unvalidated' — an inventory slot, not a guarantee.

changelog.change: Initial manifest. Restored the MOSS exact gate on ALL fixtures (the normalized-CER<0.10 escape hatch on long is REMOVED), pinned the MOSS reference (fresh CPU capture) and both GGUF hashes, renamed the loose smoke checks (test_ggml_moss_crispasr_approx_smoke, test_starling_ggml_s1_control_matrix_smoke, test_ggml_parakeet_external_text_gate) so they cannot be mistaken for accuracy certification, and inventoried every remaining test_ggml_parity.py gate as validated/unvalidated.
changelog.justification: Issue #167: docs/ggml-engine.md claimed exact MOSS text/token parity while the test accepted normalized CER<0.10 on the long fixture. Resolution (measured on CPU, 2026-09-19, against the freshly pinned reference): re-captured the reference with scripts/moss_golden.py (device=cpu, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.15.0, repo revision 82f0715, reference module clean; per-fixture output hashes pinned in this manifest and recorded in golden/moss_reference_provenance.json) — the in-tree ENGINE then reproduces short/medium/long byte-exactly (normalized CER 0.0000; 31/89/187 tokens, 121/363/737 chars). The old CER headroom was guarding a STALE reference, not engine drift. Component gates re-staged from the same pinned reference (device=cpu, ids asserted equal to the text-golden stream before staging) and re-measured: mel worst 40/951680 mismatching bins (long), worst ULP excess 0, max_abs 0.00390625 (bound: <=64 bins at <=1 bf16 ULP); encoder_hidden worst max-abs 0.01171875 (long; bound 0.02), audio_embeds worst 0.000354766846 (long; bound 0.001); qwen_decode merged embeds 100% bitwise on all fixtures, prefill argmax exact, prefill logits max-abs 0.696228/0.3695984/5.014769 (short/medium/long; bound 8.0), token stream + text EXACT on short — on CPU medium/long token streams diverge from the python eager reference (near-tie bf16 argmax flips: cpp/moss/llm.cpp documents 'CPU bf16 GEMMs are not bit-identical to cuBLAS and are a fallback only'; verified NOT a K-step artifact — STARLING_MOSS_NOKSTEP=1 gives bit-identical failing numbers), so the exact-token contract is CUDA-scoped for medium/long (enforcement block of qwen_decode.shared_fixture.token_stream) while CPU text exactness is carried by moss.intree.text (measured byte-exact on all fixtures). Parakeet long-fixture corpus gates (ratio>=0.90, content-token match>=0.65) are carried over UNCHANGED from the pre-existing tests and are now the documented approximate path in both manifest and docs (the docs previously overclaimed 'byte-exact on short/medium/long'); their goldens were absent at authoring time, so their reference blocks are explicitly unpinned (hash pinning requires a recapture — follow-up).

tolerances.component: log-mel frontend (128 bins, 16 kHz, n_fft 640, hop 160)
tolerances.metric: bin-wise equality with a per-bin bf16-ULP bound (ULP measured at each bin's own magnitude, not a global constant)
tolerances.aggregation: per-fixture mismatch count + worst ULP excess, all three fixtures must pass
tolerances.normalization: none — raw staged f32 tensors (golden/raw/moss_<fixture>_mel.f32, exact bf16-quantized values preserved)
tolerances.margin: <= 64 mismatching bins out of ~951,680 per fixture, each within 1 bf16 ULP; no non-finite output
tolerances.justification: STFT/filterbank rounding differs between torch (staged reference) and the C++ mel frontend; measured worst-case on the pinned CPU reference leaves orders of magnitude of headroom (see the moss_mel_test output recorded in PR validation). Enforced by build/moss_mel_test.

tolerances.justification: the adapter is a shallow projection over the encoder hidden state, so the tolerance is much tighter than the encoder's; measured on the pinned CPU reference with large headroom. Enforced by build/moss_encoder_test.

tolerances.component: merged inputs_embeds (token embeds + scattered audio embeds)
tolerances.metric: bitwise equality (fraction of equal elements must be 100%)
tolerances.aggregation: per-fixture, all elements; exact shape + finiteness required
tolerances.justification: embedding lookup + masked_scatter are exact integer-indexed gathers plus bf16-rounded matmuls that reproduce bitwise on a fixed backend; any drift here is a real graph bug. Measured 100.000% on all three fixtures (CPU, pinned reference). Enforced by build/moss_llm_test.

tolerances.metric: max-abs difference vs the staged eager reference
tolerances.aggregation: per-fixture max over the vocab; exact width + finiteness required
tolerances.justification: bf16 ULP compounding across the prefill layers makes bitwise logits infeasible; measured 0.696228 / 0.3695984 / 5.014769 (short/medium/long, CPU pinned reference; historically <= 3.75 on CUDA). The ARGMAX below is the correctness gate; 8.0 is a sanity ceiling. Enforced by build/moss_llm_test.

tolerances.metric: exact equality of the argmax token id
tolerances.justification: the prefill argmax seeds the greedy decode; a wrong seed token cannot recover downstream. Measured exact on all three fixtures. Enforced by build/moss_llm_test.

cpu.note: cpp/moss/llm.cpp documents the decoder's byte-exactness contract as CUDA-scoped: 'CPU bf16 GEMMs are not bit-identical to cuBLAS and are a fallback only'. Measured on CPU against the pinned reference: short exact; medium/long diverge at near-tie argmax positions (NOT a K-step artifact — STARLING_MOSS_NOKSTEP=1 reproduces the bit-identical failing numbers). On CPU those fixtures' id/text columns are REPORTED, not gated; end-to-end CPU text exactness is carried by moss.intree.text (measured byte-exact on all three fixtures). Any other backend (Vulkan/Metal/...) gets the full strict gate.
